# Merge GHRmodels

## Description

This function stack together two or more objects `GHRmodels` object, returning one `GHRmodels` object that contains **all** the input models. All models included in the stack must have the same family, outcome, and data. If any `model_id` is duplicated across the inputs the `new_name` argument must be provided to ensure unique IDs.

```r
stack_models(..., new_name = NULL, vs_first = FALSE)
```

## Arguments

- `...`: Two or more `GHRmodels` objects, or a single list of them.
- `new_name`: `NULL` (default) or a character used to build the new model IDs.
- `vs_first`: Logical. If TRUE columns comparing the model vs the first model are kept in the `mod_gof`, otherwise are discarded. Default is FALSE. Set to TRUE only when models contained in the `GHRmodels` object to be stacked are compared with the same first models.

## Details

Combine (Stack) Multiple GHRmodels Objects

## Returns

A single `GHRmodels` object containing all models from the inputs.

## See Also

`subset_models` for subsetting GHRmodels objects, `fit_models` for fitting INLA models.

## Examples

```r
data(dengue_MS)
dengue_MS <- dengue_MS[dengue_MS$year %in% 2010:2012, ]

# Formulas
formulas1 <- "dengue_cases ~ tmin + f(month, model='rw2')"
formulas2 <- "dengue_cases ~ tmax + f(month, model='rw2')"

# Fit
fitmod1 <- fit_models(
  formulas = formulas1,
  data = dengue_MS,
  family = "nbinomial",
  offset_var = "pop100000"
)
fitmod2 <- fit_models(
  formulas = formulas2,
  data = dengue_MS,
  family = "nbinomial",
  offset_var = "pop100000"
)

# Stack
stacked <- stack_models(fitmod1, fitmod2, new_name = "mod")
```
